comment: Koog calls kotlin.jvm.internal.Reflection.typeOf(Class) on these types (storage keys, node IO types, feature keys). When full kotlin-reflect is active in the native image (it is in bosca-server, for the scripting engine), typeOf eagerly deserializes each class's @Metadata; unregistered classes throw KotlinReflectionInternalError 'Unresolved class'. List derived by scanning all ai.koog jvm jars for Reflection.typeOf call sites. ALSO: the Item/GooglePart hierarchies are registered because koog's OpenAI and Google clients encode request bodies via JsonContentPolymorphicSerializer, whose serialize() resolves the runtime subtype's serializer reflectively (Companion field -> serializer() method). Unregistered subtypes fail in native with kotlinx 'Class X is not registered for polymorphic serialization in the scope of Y' (misleading message; the reflective lookup returned null). These are the only two JsonContentPolymorphicSerializer hierarchies in koog 1.1.1/1.1.1-beta. ALSO: top-level request/response DTOs of every koog provider client (+Companions) are registered because KtorKoogHttpClient.post/sse serializes bodies with setBody(value, TypeInfo(KClass)) and decodes with body(TypeInfo(KClass)) - ktor resolves those serializers via the reflective KClass.serializerOrNull() Companion lookup, and streaming uses reified decodeFromString (runtime typeOf). List = every ai.koog class constant fed to Reflection.getOrCreateKotlinClass/typeOf inside *Client classes across all provider jars.
